strategy_objective_guidance:
- The evaluator has a single scored term: `combined_score = (min over 286 triangle areas / ConvexHull area) / 0.030936889034895654`. Everything else (eval_time is reported but not scored; no penalty) is irrelevant except hard validity: must return a finite NumPy array of shape (13,2) and `ConvexHull(points)` must not fail (non-degenerate 2D hull). Any exception → score 0.
- The objective is invariant to similarity/affine transforms and translation, so fix a normalization (e.g., hull area = 1, centroid at origin) to remove null directions and improve optimizer conditioning.
- This is a pure max-min problem over 26 continuous variables; the minimum is non-smooth (piecewise-linear in coordinates, since areas are |determinants|). The binding constraint is the single smallest triangle — the largest remaining lever is directly raising that active minimum, which typically has few active triples (often 1–5). There are no competing weighted sub-scores and no term rewarding anything other than the nominal goal.
- The program receives no input at all — it is a pure offline/batch computation. This permits arbitrary multistart, long deterministic optimization, and precomputed structure, subject only to the timeout. Nothing must be causal/streaming.
- Key risk: score 0 on any crash or degenerate hull — always wrap optimizers in try/except and return the best valid incumbent; ensure no duplicate points and hull dimension 2 before returning.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Smooth-surrogate max-min: replace min with soft-min (log-sum-exp) over the 286 areas and maximize via `scipy.optimize.minimize` (L-BFGS-B / SLSQP) with analytic gradients of the determinant areas; anneal the temperature down. Mechanism: converts the non-smooth min into a differentiable objective the optimizer can actually follow.
- Direct non-smooth local optimization: maximize the exact min via `scipy.optimize.minimize` with Nelder-Mead or Powell on the 26 variables (no gradient needed, robust to kinks), from many deterministic starts. Mechanism: exact objective, no surrogate bias.
- Active-set / cutting-plane method: identify the (few) triples attaining the minimum, optimize only those areas (maximize min of active set) with constraints, re-solve as the active set changes. Formulate as an LP/QP-like problem via `scipy.optimize.linprog` or SLSQP with area constraints on active triples. Mechanism: the min is determined by few triples, so a small constrained problem captures the whole objective.
- Structured/parametric families: place points on a parametric curve or symmetric pattern (regular 13-gon perturbations, ring + interior point layouts, symmetric orbits under a dihedral group) and optimize the few shape parameters. Mechanism: drastically reduces dimension, gives strong deterministic starts; known Heilbronn-type optima are often symmetric.
- Deterministic multistart with fixed RNG seeds: generate diverse seeds via low-discrepancy sequences (`numpy.random.SeedSequence` with fixed seeds, or explicit Halton-like construction) inside the hull, run local polish from each, keep global best. Mechanism: max-min landscape is multimodal; multistart is the standard global lever, fully deterministic.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Refinement of the smooth-surrogate approach: temperature schedule e.g. soft-min temperature from ~1e-2 down to 1e-6 of hull area, L-BFGS-B with `ftol=1e-12, gtol=1e-10, maxiter=2000` per temperature; at the end, one exact active-set polish on the argmin triple.
- Active-set polish: after local optimum, take triples with area within 1e-9 of the min, solve max t s.t. area_i ≥ t for active i (SLSQP), iterate until active set stabilizes (typically <10 rounds).
- Normalization discipline: after each optimizer step, re-center to centroid and rescale so hull area = 1; this prevents drift into degenerate configurations and keeps gradients well-scaled.
- Incumbent management: cache best-so-far (points, score) after every successful stage; on any optimizer exception or non-finite output, return cached incumbent — never let a failed polish zero the score.
- Budget control: target total runtime well under timeout (e.g., 5–20 s): allocate ~50–200 local runs of ≤0.1 s each; verify hull validity (`ConvexHull` succeeds, min pairwise distance > 1e-9) before accepting a candidate as incumbent.
- Symmetry-breaking initialization: start from a regular 13-gon on the unit circle plus deterministic radial perturbations of alternating sign/magnitude — empirically strong baselines for convex Heilbronn; then perturb each point independently by a decaying schedule (σ: 0.1 → 1e-6) accepting only improvements (deterministic hill-climb on the exact objective).

strategies.title: [softmin-annealed-multistart] Soft-min surrogate annealing with exact active-set
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: smooth-surrogate max-min optimization (log-sum-exp annealing + active-set polish)
Replacement scope: Replace the entire body of `heilbronn_convex13()` (the random `rng.random` construction) with a deterministic multistart soft-min annealing pipeline followed by an exact active-set polish.
Compute budget: ≤ 24 deterministic starts (regular 13-gon plus 23 fixed-seed perturbations of it); per start ≤ 600 L-BFGS-B iterations across 6 annealing temperatures (100 each) plus ≤ 8 SLSQP active-set rounds of ≤ 200 iterations; expected total runtime 5–15 s, well within timeout.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's min normalized triangle area (0.000322) is essentially that of uniform random points, where many near-collinear triples exist. The new degree of freedom is direct gradient-based control over the smallest triangle areas: the log-sum-exp soft-min is differentiable with analytic gradients of the 286 determinant areas, so the optimizer can raise the binding minimum instead of leaving it to chance. The incumbent (pure RNG) has zero exploitation of the objective; this strategy directly optimizes it.
Plan: (1) Compute all 286 index triples once. Define area_i = |det(p_b − p_a, p_c − p_a)|/2 for each triple, and normalize by fixing the convex-hull area to 1 after each stage (re-center centroid, rescale so `ConvexHull(points).volume == 1`). (2) Starts: start 0 is the regular 13-gon on the unit circle (this alone already beats random configurations for convex Heilbronn); starts 1–23 perturb the 13-gon with fixed deterministic offsets (seeded `np.random.default_rng(k)`, σ = 0.05, plus alternating radial perturbations ±0.1). (3) For each start, run L-BFGS-B (`ftol=1e-12, gtol=1e-10`) maximizing the soft-min −T·log Σ exp(−area_i/T) for T ∈ {1e-2, 3e-3, 1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5} (areas normalized by hull area), with analytic gradient d(softmin)/dp_j = Σ softmax-weighted ∇area_i; keep the best exact-min configuration at each temperature. (4) After annealing, exact active-set polish: take triples within 1e-9 of the current min, maximize t s.t. area_i ≥ t for those triples via SLSQP over the 26 coordinates plus t, re-identify the active set, repeat until stable (≤ 8 rounds). (5) Track the global best exact normalized min across all starts; wrap every optimizer call in try/except; before accepting any candidate verify all points finite, min pairwise distance > 1e-9, and `ConvexHull` succeeds. Return the best incumbent; if all optimization fails, return the regular 13-gon (valid, non-degenerate hull). Expected-gain check: the regular 13-gon alone has a computable normalized minimum triangle area far above the incumbent's 0.000322 (its smallest triangles use three adjacent vertices and have normalized area ≈ 0.5·sin(2π/13)·(1 − cos(2π/13)) / (13/2 · sin(2π/13)) ≈ 0.013, i.e. combined_score ≈ 0.42), and the annealing/polish stages only increase it, so this strategy strictly exceeds the current 0.010423 by more than an order of magnitude.

strategies.title: [ring-plus-interior-orbits] Dihedral-symmetric parametric family: 12-gon ring pl
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: structured parametric family with reduced dimensionality (symmetric orbits under cyclic group)
Replacement scope: Replaces the point-generation phase entirely; the local optimizer operates only on the family's shape parameters, not on all 26 coordinates.
Compute budget: One parametric family with ≤ 8 free parameters; ≤ 40 deterministic parameter starts (grid over radii/phase offsets); ≤ 400 Nelder-Mead iterations per start (dimension ≤ 8, cheap); expected runtime < 3 s.
Gain mechanism: The new degree of freedom is a contact-topology change: instead of 13 comparable points, use 12 points on a slightly irregular ring plus 1 interior point. With a center point present, the binding triples change from adjacent-vertex slivers to (center, two adjacent ring points) and (three nearby ring points), which the ring radius profile can balance; the incumbent (random points) cannot realize any balanced contact structure at all.
Plan: (1) Construct points as p_0 = (0,0) and p_k = r(θ_k)·(cos θ_k, sin θ_k) for k = 1..12 with θ_k = 2π(k−1)/12 + φ (one phase parameter φ). Use a radius profile r(θ) = 1 + a·cos(12θ/2) + b·sin(12θ/2) restricted to ≤ 3 low-frequency Fourier modes (total ≤ 8 parameters: φ, 3 Fourier amplitudes, plus optionally a small offset of the center point). (2) Grid-search the amplitudes (a ∈ [−0.15, 0.15] in 5 steps per mode, φ ∈ {0, π/12}) to get ≤ 40 deterministic starts, evaluating the exact normalized min (286 determinant areas divided by hull area). (3) Polish the best few configurations with Nelder-Mead on the ≤ 8 parameters (exact non-smooth objective, `xatol=1e-10, fatol=1e-12`), keeping the best. (4) Validity: the ring with |a|,|b| ≤ 0.15 keeps all 12 ring points on a star-shaped curve around the origin with distinct angles, so no duplicates; the hull is the ring (non-degenerate, area > 0); the center point is strictly interior, which is allowed since points may lie inside the convex region. Wrap in try/except, fall back to the best grid candidate. Expected-gain check: the mechanism is the new balanced contact topology (center-point triples whose areas are directly tunable via the radius profile) which the incumbent's random configuration cannot achieve; a falsifiable threshold is combined_score > 0.010423 (normalized min area > 0.000322), and the 12-gon-plus-center baseline itself already yields normalized min area on the order of 10⁻³–10⁻² (center-adjacent-adjacent triangles have area ≈ ½·r²·sin(π/6) ≈ 0.125·r² before normalization vs. hull area ≈ 3r², i.e. ≈ 0.04 normalized), so the predicted combined_score ≈ 1.0–1.3 strictly exceeds the incumbent.

strategies.title: Mechanism family: exact-objective stochastic-restart hill-climbing with explicit
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: exact-objective stochastic-restart hill-climbing with explicit topological escape moves (vertex↔interior role exchange)
Replacement scope: Replaces the construction with a hill-climb loop over the full 26 coordinates, seeded from the best of several deterministic topologies, with a specific escape move the incumbent lacks.
Compute budget: ≤ 6 seeds (regular 13-gon; 12-gon+center; 11-gon+2 interior on a diameter; 10-gon+3 interior; two fixed-seed quasi-random Sobol sets via `scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol`); per seed ≤ 3000 accepted-or-rejected single-point perturbation trials with σ decaying 0.05 → 1e-6 geometrically; expected runtime < 5 s.
Gain mechanism: The escape move — reassigning a hull vertex to the interior and vice versa — changes the contact topology (which triples are near-collinear and which points bound the hull), a degree of freedom no gradient method or single fixed layout can cross; the incumbent random draw has no search at all.
Plan: (1) Seed set as listed; evaluate exact normalized min for each (286 determinants / hull area). (2) Hill-climb: at each step perturb one point by Gaussian σ (fixed seed per seed-index for determinism), accept iff the exact normalized min strictly improves and validity holds (finite, min pairwise distance > 1e-9, `ConvexHull` succeeds); decay σ by factor 0.997 per rejection, reset to 0.02 every 500 trials as a deterministic restart-within-run. (3) Every 600 trials, attempt one topological escape: pick the hull vertex participating in the most minimum-area triples and move it to the centroid of the interior points scaled by 0.5, or move the interior point farthest from all active triples onto the hull boundary midpoint of its two nearest hull neighbors; accept only if the exact objective improves after 50 follow-up micro-perturbations at σ = 0.01. (4) Keep the global best across seeds; wrap all in try/except with incumbent caching; return the best valid configuration, falling back to the regular 13-gon if everything fails. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is explicit hull/interior role exchange that lets the search cross between contact topologies (e.g., 13-vertex hulls vs. 12-vertex hulls with one interior point), which the incumbent's single random draw cannot do; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 0.010423, with the regular-13-gon seed alone already guaranteeing ≈ 0.42 as computed in strategy 1, so the returned configuration strictly exceeds the incumbent.
